assumptions.description: LLM claims are advisory until deterministic gates pass.

components.name: Configuration & Settings
responsibilities: Load and validate runtime configuration (FMC host, credentials, timeouts) as typed pydantic settings consumed by client and server.

components.name: FMC HTTP Client (auth, transport, token cache)
responsibilities: Own async HTTP transport to the FMC REST API, base64 basic-auth handshake, and time-based auth-token caching/refresh.

components.name: MCP Tool Surface
responsibilities: Retrieve FMC domain objects via the HTTP client and expose them as MCP tools with IP-address input validation.

components.name: MCP Server Runtime & Entrypoint
responsibilities: Construct the FastMCP server, wire config and client into its lifecycle, and expose the process entrypoint that launches the server.

invariants.description: All component, contract, and gap claims must trace to selected graph nodes/edges and their provenance; no responsibilities, tools, or endpoints may be invented beyond packet evidence.
Acceptance must be deterministic; the client's time-based token caching and any wall-clock or network ordering must be controlled/stubbed so the pytest suite yields stable results.
Every owned node, supporting edge, and check is anchored to packet provenance ids so the decomposition is auditable back to the source graph.
Acceptance must not call the live FMC controller or require credentials; the httpx-based client and FastMCP runtime must be exercised offline with stubs, per project non-goals.

nearNeighborAlternatives.description: Split the client into a separate authentication/token-cache component and a thin HTTP transport component.
nearNeighborAlternatives.whyNotPrimary: Auth (base64), token caching (time), and transport (httpx) are co-located in the single client module with no edge evidence of a distinct auth surface; splitting would create sub-file fragments rather than independent responsibility units. Anchored to goal: decompose the Cisco FMC MCP server into responsibility-bearing components that can be manually evaluated by Leon; non-goals: do not require live FMC credentials or network calls for acceptance; do not accept file-bucket components.

nearNeighborAlternatives.description: Merge tools and resources into a single 'FMC operations' component.
nearNeighborAlternatives.whyNotPrimary: Responsibilities differ: resources retrieve and serialize FMC data via the client, while tools define the MCP tool surface and own input validation (ipaddress); the tools->resources import edge confirms a layered dependency, not a single unit. Anchored to goal: decompose the Cisco FMC MCP server into responsibility-bearing components that can be manually evaluated by Leon; non-goals: do not require live FMC credentials or network calls for acceptance; do not accept file-bucket components.

nearNeighborAlternatives.description: Treat fmc_mcp.__main__ as its own standalone entrypoint component separate from the server runtime.
nearNeighborAlternatives.whyNotPrimary: __main__ only imports and delegates to fmc_mcp.server (single import edge) and carries no independent responsibility; isolating it would produce a rejected file-bucket component. Anchored to goal: decompose the Cisco FMC MCP server into responsibility-bearing components that can be manually evaluated by Leon; non-goals: do not require live FMC credentials or network calls for acceptance; do not accept file-bucket components.

risks.description: A fluent decomposition could optimize the wrong target; near-neighbors and probes mitigate this.
risks.mitigation: Run deterministic gates, held-out probes, and independent review.

verificationGaps.description: No selected edge connects fmc_mcp.server to fmc_mcp.tools, so registration/exposure of MCP tools through the server runtime is not observable from the graph; the tool surface may be wired via decorators or runtime registration not captured by the packet.
verificationGaps.proposedClosureCheck: Add an offline check that imports fmc_mcp.server and asserts the expected FMC tools are registered on the FastMCP instance.

verificationGaps.description: Client FMC HTTP/auth behavior (httpx transport, base64 basic auth, time-based token caching) cannot be exercised against a live controller under the no-network/no-credentials acceptance constraint, so the real FMC request contract is verified only via mocks/offline.
verificationGaps.proposedClosureCheck: Add offline contract tests that stub the httpx transport and assert request shaping, auth header construction, and token-cache expiry logic.

verificationGaps.description: The fmc_mcp.__main__ -> fmc_mcp.server startup path (process entrypoint) is not shown to be covered by tests in the packet.
verificationGaps.proposedClosureCheck: Add a smoke test invoking the module entrypoint with a stubbed server.run to assert it starts without network.

verificationGaps.description: Documentation/static surfaces present in the graph (markdown_section x45 with 45 documents edges) and config surfaces (config x3 with 3 configures edges) were not selected and are not componentized, so their accuracy and coverage remain undecomposed.
verificationGaps.proposedClosureCheck: Select documentation and config nodes in a follow-up packet and either map them to owning components or emit explicit doc-accuracy checks.
